title: One carbon more
hook: Count the atoms and trace their bonds.

knows: Condensed structural formulas and covalent bonds.
doesNotKnow: The first structure has formula C₂H₆O; the second has CH₄O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.

misconception: Different-looking structural drawings must represent different formulas or different compounds.
objective: Compare molecular formula and connectivity when classifying two structures.

claims.text: Structure A is ethanol (C₂H₆O); structure B is methanol (CH₄O). The first structure has formula C₂H₆O; the second has CH₄O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.
Constitutional isomers have the same molecular formula but different atomic connectivity.
The diagrams show condensed connectivity, not stereochemistry or molecular geometry.
Recall: What relationship do ethanol and methanol have? The first structure has formula C₂H₆O; the second has CH₄O. Because the atom counts differ, this pair is not a pair of constitutional isomers.
